messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — continuous-batching latency spike detected on inference-runtime cluster-west-1. 95th p99 tokens/sec dropping, queue depth increasing. Paging on-call.
Alex Carter: I see it — dashboards show continuous_batching queue piling and KV cache eviction rate jumped. Customer-facing latency > 2s for some requests.
Maria Nguyen: Which model tiers? Hosted or Dedicated?
Alex Carter: Primarily hosted L model pool and a few Dedicated shards hitting bursty concurrent traffic. High concurrency + long prefixes seems to be thrashing KV cache and causing batching to coalesce into huge microbatches.
Ben Li: Repro: run a 500 qps synthetic with sticky keys and you get batch sizes hitting 512, then GC/eviction. Keyspace hot spots.
Sophie K: Tags: perf-cliff, thundering-herd, kv-blowup. Impact: multiple customers reporting timeouts and function-call failures.
Alex Carter: Mitigation attempt 1: reduced max_microbatch_size from 512 -> 128 on runtime group west-1. Doing rolling patch now.
Alex Carter: Command I used:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap inference-runtime-config -p '{"data":{"max_microbatch_size":"128"}}'
# then rolling restart of runtime pods on west-1 nodepool
```
Maria Nguyen: Seeing immediate drop in average batch size on one shard, but queue latency still elevated for some nodes. Seems like jittering is not uniform.
Ben Li: While Alex patches, I'm going to toggle continuous batching fallback to disabled for the most impacted model family to force single-request mode: this will spike CPU but should reduce cache pressure.
Sophie K: Customer impact note: voice.ai and client-42 had ~15% error rate on generation calls between 07:42-07:54 UTC. Created support tickets and flagged for priority.
Oncall Rotation Bot: Handoff reminder: Alex -> Maria at 08:00 UTC. Maria will take lead if issue persists.
Alex Carter: Patch rolled everywhere. Also applied a temporary per-customer concurrency cap of 60 for hosted tier to reduce bursts.
Maria Nguyen: Taking lead. Running a KV cache diagnostic: top keys show hotset concentrated on a few long-prefix customers. I propose enabling prefix-level TTL to drop stale KV quickly and increase kv-cache-max-entries to avoid thrash? Thoughts?
Ben Li: Prefix TTL might help but it's risky for correctness. Prefer immediate safer steps: increase jitter variance and enable per-request jitter on enqueuing to avoid synchronized arrivals.
Maria Nguyen: Good call. I'll apply enqueue jitter config: set enqueue_jitter_ms = 20-200 in runtime config. Command:
```json
{"enqueue_jitter_ms":"20-200"}
```
Ben Li: Also enabling kvcache eviction smoothing: set eviction_rate_limit=1000/s -> will avoid mass evicts.
Sophie K: Ops note for postmortem — capture a sample of request ids for voice.ai for root cause. Also send templated customer update.
Alex Carter: Quick fallback plan if things worsen: revert batching enabled -> false across affected clusters. That is heavy but restores latency predictability.
Maria Nguyen: After jitter+max_microbatch change, p95 reduced from 1.9s -> 700ms on most shards, p99 still around 1.5s on a couple nodes. Error rate dropping.
Ben Li: I'm seeing a node in west-1b still accumulating large KV churn. I'm SSHing into it to inspect disk IO and GC logs.
Alex Carter: On the support side, CS sent an interim message to voice.ai explaining mitigation steps and ETA for full stabilization.
Oncall Rotation Bot: Reminder: incident severity still P1. Please update incident board.
Maria Nguyen: Handoff to Sophie at 08:15 UTC if all good. Sophie, I'm marking the issue as mitigated but not resolved — need config PRs to make changes permanent and add canaries for microbatch-size changes.
Sophie K: I'll own the PRs and the postmortem. Action items: 1) config PR to make jitter default 20-200ms with canary rollout, 2) add per-model concurrency caps, 3) export kv-cache eviction metrics to SLO dashboard, 4) customer writeups.
Ben Li: Also add an automated detection rule: rapid rise in eviction rate + growing mean batch size => auto-rollback batching config or reduce max_microbatch_size.
Alex Carter: Thanks team. I'll follow up with support ticket updates. Leaving a note: avoided full rollback; used microbatch cap + jitter + per-customer throttle.
Sophie K: :thumbsup: taking postmortem + closing loop on ownership. Will schedule a runbook update for thundering-herd scenarios.
incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 08:12 UTC by Maria Nguyen. Duration: 30m.
Maria Nguyen: Last check: p99 tokens/sec trending back to baseline. Closing the immediate incident. Will reopen if regressions show up.
